title: File:Sarras vigne et village.jpg
author: François Bassaget
description: Sarras vue partielle -- Syrah vines in autumn colour on the hillside above Sarras, Ardèche, with the village and the Rhône below. Sarras is a Saint-Joseph AOC commune.
sourcing_note: Found via commune-level search (Sarras), not the AOC name -- 'Saint-Joseph' as a search term on Commons returns almost nothing but the Catholic saint and EU regulatory PDFs. Category:Saint-Joseph (AOC) has 0 members. This is the pattern to repeat for any future Saint-Joseph sourcing: search by commune (Mauves, Tournon-sur-Rhône, Saint-Jean-de-Muzols, Sarras, Chavanay, Charnas, Saint-Désirat), never by the appellation name.

title: File:Les vignes.jpg
author: Mr Fougerolle
description: les vignes de Chanos-Curson -- flat, fertile vineyard plain at Chanos-Curson, a confirmed Crozes-Hermitage AOC commune (one of the 11 communes named in the appellation decree). Aerial/elevated view showing the characteristic deeper, more fertile soils and flat terrain that distinguish Crozes-Hermitage from Hermitage's steep granite slope.
sourcing_note: Same commune-search pattern as Saint-Peray and Saint-Joseph: 'Crozes-Hermitage' as a search term is drowned out by EU Official Journal PDFs (the AOC name appears in hundreds of multilingual regulatory filings). The whole Crozes-Hermitage Commons category has only 7 files, none usable. Direct commune searches (Larnage, Gervans, Mercurol, Beaumont-Monteux, Pont-de-l'Isere) also came up empty -- mostly civic/administrative content. The find came from Category:Vineyards in Drome, a small (12-file) but well-curated category that doesn't surface on name-based searches at all. Worth checking 'Vineyards in <department>' categories before concluding a commune search has failed.

title: Pexels stock photo -- vineyard at golden hour
author: Anna Hinckel
description: A scenic view of a vibrant vineyard during sunset, showcasing lush green foliage. No specific location given by the photographer -- used as a general Rhone-valley-appropriate cover image, not as a claim about a specific site.
sourcing_note: Steve rejected nr_tain_rhone as the cover/loop photo (wanted 'a more beautiful shot'). Commons search for a dramatic golden-hour Rhone shot hit repeated rate-limit errors (HTTP 429) this session and the searches that did complete returned nothing beyond what was already in the library (all checked and rejected as not beautiful enough -- see build commit). Moved to Pexels via the project's existing fetch_pexels.py / PEXELS_API_KEY pattern (sourcing/fetch_pexels.py, documented in guides/SETUP_KEYS.md).

title: Pexels stock photo -- French vineyard, autumn
author: Alisa Skripina
description: Scenic view of vineyards in France during autumn, with picturesque rural landscape -- photographer gives no specific commune or AOC. Used as an explicitly generic 'lifestyle' stand-in for Saint-Joseph, per Steve's own instruction, not asserted as an authentic Saint-Joseph vineyard.
sourcing_note: Replaces nr_saintjoseph_sarras_vigne (1250x940, too soft at reel crop -- Steve's call). Steve explicitly authorized a Pexels lifestyle shot as fallback if authentic Saint-Joseph photography couldn't be found at better resolution; two other strong candidates from the same Pexels search (a misty terraced valley, a lakeside terraced slope) were rejected despite being more dramatic because they are Koge, Denmark and Lavaux, Switzerland respectively -- using either for a 'Saint-Joseph' beat would have been a geography error, not just an authenticity compromise Steve already signed off on.
